newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI sets terms for new stock exchanges.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI sets terms for new stock exchanges.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Tuesday that it would recognise new stock exchanges provided they used screen-based trading, adopted rules to protect investors and had clearing houses.
SEBI said in a statement that recognition, if considered necessary in the public interest and that of the trade, would be subject to the following conditions:
- The exchange begins trading only after introduction of on-line screen-based trading.
- The exchange makes rules, regulations and by-laws with adequate provisions for investor protection with the approval of SEBI and thereafter strictly follows them.
- The exchange establishes a clearing house within six months from the date of its recognition.
"The view was that SEBI could regulate but not prohibit new exchanges," SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told reporters after the board meeting.
